doc.title: Billy Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Life on the road and dance music
summary: Adverse conditions everywhere; dancing and jazz were inseparable.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: What was it like being on the road in that time? Was it different when you went from one part of the country to the other going from north to south?

Yeah. Well yes there’s a difference. But you find adverse conditions shall we say, anywhere. You know the geographical locations didn’t necessarily dictate to what the social or accepted mores of the community might be you know.
And the majority of the gigs that you played were for dances still at that time? It seems like dancing was a very big part of jazz music at that time.
